source.text: If the JWT could be used in an application context in which it could be confused with other kinds of JWTs, then mitigations MUST be employed to prevent these substitution attacks.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Libraries MUST enable the caller to specify a supported set of algorithms and MUST NOT use any other algorithms when performing cryptographic operations.

notes: multiple keywords in one sentence; split into one requirement each
contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: The library MUST ensure that the "alg" or "enc" header specifies the same algorithm that is used for the cryptographic operation.
Moreover, each key MUST be used with exactly one algorithm, and this MUST be checked when the cryptographic operation is performed.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Even if a JWS can be successfully validated, unless the algorithm(s) used in the JWS are acceptable to the application, it SHOULD consider the JWS to be invalid."

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Therefore, applications MUST only allow the use of cryptographically current algorithms that meet the security requirements of the application.
Applications MUST therefore be designed to enable cryptographic agility.
JWT libraries SHOULD NOT generate JWTs using "none" unless explicitly requested to do so by the caller.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Similarly, JWT libraries SHOULD NOT consume JWTs using "none" unless explicitly requested by the caller.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Applications SHOULD follow these algorithm-specific recommendations:
To counter these attacks, JWT libraries SHOULD implement ECDSA using the deterministic approach defined in [RFC6979].
All cryptographic operations used in the JWT MUST be validated and the entire JWT MUST be rejected if any of them fail to validate.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: This is true not only of JWTs with a single set of Header Parameters but also for Nested JWTs in which both outer and inner operations MUST be validated using the keys and algorithms supplied by the application.

For the NIST prime-order curves P-256, P-384, and P-521, validation MUST be performed according to Section 5.6.2.3.4 (ECC Partial Public-Key Validation Routine) of "Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key-Establishment Schemes Using Discrete Logarithm Cryptography" [nist-sp-800-56a-r3].

source.section_title: Ensure Cryptographic Keys Have Sufficient Entropy
source.text: The Key Entropy and Random Values advice in Section 10.1 of [RFC7515] and the Password Considerations in Section 8.8 of [RFC7518] MUST be followed.

source.section_title: Ensure Cryptographic Keys Have Sufficient Entropy
source.text: In particular, human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be directly used as the key to a keyed-MAC algorithm such as "HS256".
Compression of data SHOULD NOT be done before encryption, because such compressed data often reveals information about the plaintext.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Implementations and applications MUST do this and not use or admit the use of other Unicode encodings for these purposes.
When a JWT contains an "iss" (issuer) claim, the application MUST validate that the cryptographic keys used for the cryptographic operations in the JWT belong to the issuer.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: If they do not, the application MUST reject the JWT.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Similarly, when the JWT contains a "sub" (subject) claim, the application MUST validate that the subject value corresponds to a valid subject and/or issuer-subject pair at the application.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: If the issuer, subject, or the pair are invalid, the application MUST reject the JWT.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: If the same issuer can issue JWTs that are intended for use by more than one relying party or application, the JWT MUST contain an "aud" (audience) claim that can be used to determine whether the JWT is being used by an intended party or was substituted by an attacker at an unintended party.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: In such cases, the relying party or application MUST validate the audience value, and if the audience value is not present or not associated with the recipient, it MUST reject the JWT.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Applications SHOULD protect against such attacks, e.g., by matching the URL to a whitelist of allowed locations and ensuring no cookies are sent in the GET request.
Per the definition of "typ" in Section 4.1.9 of [RFC7515], it is RECOMMENDED that the "application/" prefix be omitted from the "typ" value.
Therefore, for example, the "typ" value used to explicitly include a type for a SET SHOULD be "secevent+jwt".

When explicit typing is employed for a JWT, it is RECOMMENDED that a media type name of the format "application/example+jwt" be used, where "example" is replaced by the identifier for the specific kind of JWT.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: When applying explicit typing to a Nested JWT, the "typ" Header Parameter containing the explicit type value MUST be present in the inner JWT of the Nested JWT (the JWT whose payload is the JWT Claims Set).

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Explicit typing is RECOMMENDED for new uses of JWTs.

source.section_title: Use Mutually Exclusive Validation Rules for Different Kinds of
source.text: If more than one kind of JWT can be issued by the same issuer, the validation rules for those JWTs MUST be written such that they are mutually exclusive, rejecting JWTs of the wrong kind.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.section_title: Use Mutually Exclusive Validation Rules for Different Kinds of
source.text: As discussed in Section 3.11, for new JWT applications, the use of explicit typing is RECOMMENDED.
